payload.title: Wedding Without a Seating Chart and How to Make It Work
payload.excerpt: When open seating suits your wedding and when it backfires, the middle ground between a full chart and free seating, and how to brief your venue, MC and caterer so every guest is looked after, at home or abroad.
key_takeaways: No rule says a wedding needs a seating chart, so the decision rests on the meal service, the room and how well your guests know each other.
Open seating suits cocktail receptions, shared or station dinners, one long table and welcome events, and struggles with plated meals, blended families and guests who need extra care.
Reserving tables for family and elders, or assigning tables rather than seats, keeps the relaxed feel while looking after the people who matter.
Across a destination wedding weekend, open seating at welcome drinks and a planned seating arrangement at the wedding dinner can sit comfortably side by side.

faq.q: Is it okay to not have assigned seating at a wedding?
faq.a: Yes. It suits cocktail receptions, shared or station dinners, small weddings and guest lists who know each other. Reserve seats for family and elders, set extra chairs and tell guests in advance.

faq.q: What to do instead of a seating chart?
faq.a: Assign tables rather than seats, reserve tables for family and the wedding party only, choose long feasting tables, or mix lounges and standing areas with a few dining tables.

faq.q: Do you need table numbers without a seating plan?
faq.a: Not always, but your caterer may. For plated service or special meals, ask the venue whether table numbers help the team serve the right meal to the right guest. Reserved tables still need a clear marker.

faq.q: How many extra seats do you need with no seating chart?
faq.a: There is no single figure, because it depends on the room, the table shapes and how your guests group together. Ask your venue, and expect a good answer to cover where the spare places will sit, where extra chairs are kept and who adds them on the night.

faq.q: Should the couple have their own table if there is open seating?
faq.a: Yes. Keep your own seats reserved, whether a sweetheart table, a head table with the wedding party or two places at a long table, so you never hunt for a chair.
